events.title: Lying & Manipulation with Logic
events.description: What it takes to formalize lying and untrustworthy belief in logic, from Gettier's knowledge puzzles to geometric shapes built to model networks of unreliable computers.

events.title: TTS Panel @Oedipus Craft Space: Housing the People
events.description: Why Europe's housing crisis is less about supply than lost community and trust, debunking myths about immigration and homeownership, and what historic Amsterdam and Vienna housing models still teach us.

events.title: How to Change 21st Century Minds
events.description: Why debates and protests rarely change minds, and what actually does—close relationships, lived experience, and rebuilding the everyday social spaces we've let disappear.

events.title: Listening as an Art and Learning Method
events.description: How a sound artist and a radio broadcaster explore listening as an active, collective practice, tracing deep listening's roots and jamming's power to include outsiders and challenge academic norms.

events.title: Jewish Answer to Colonialism and Barbarism
events.description: Why embracing "barbarism" and Jewish messianic thought might offer a sharper challenge to law, authority, and colonial hierarchies than conventional decolonial theory.

events.title: Feminist Approaches to Logic
events.description: How philosopher Rebecca Kosten uses Audre Lorde's writing to question whether classical logic's claim to objectivity is truly neutral, and what a feminist approach to formal reasoning could look like instead.

events.title: Hormones, Alcohol & Cognition
events.description: How gender bias in alcohol-research questionnaires leaves women and transgender people's real barriers to treatment unmeasured, and what the menstrual cycle reveals about drinking motives and cognition.

events.title: Decolonializing Decolonialization – Questions from Rabbinical Thought
events.description: How rethinking stupidity, intelligence, and civilization exposes the hidden colonial logic still shaping democracy, capitalism, and Jewish thought today.

events.title: Futuristic – To Whom? The Sound of Gqom and South African Electro Music
events.description: Josephine Zwaan discusses her research on gqom, exploring how South African producers understand rhythm, dance, and futurism differently from Western listeners who project sci-fi meaning onto the genre.

events.title: Forensic Psychology
events.description: Forensic psychologist Eva Billen on why self-control shifts over time in offenders, how researchers try to measure it, and what teen misbehavior reveals about adult self-regulation.

events.title: The Applications of Quantum Computers
events.description: A geoscientist explains how he translates earthquake and acoustic wave equations into quantum algorithms with Google, why quantum computers excel at some calculations but not others, and what breakthroughs could mean for medical imaging and subsurface exploration.

events.title: AI for Sign Language
events.description: Oline Ranum explains why translating between spoken and sign languages is such a hard AI problem, and how 3D geometry, symmetry, and linguistic structure could help models finally learn it.

events.title: Animal Spirits and Arational Behaviour
events.description: How economists separate true uncertainty from calculable risk, and why pension scenario modelling now maps a wide range of possible futures instead of forecasting one likely outcome.

events.title: Can AI Decode Sound?
events.description: How AI models trained on human speech encode sound into vectors, and what happens when those same models are used to analyze bat calls and Dutch phoneme structure.

events.title: Breaking Up the Glass Ceiling: Female Leadership in Economics
events.description: How the Women in Economics Index tracks female leadership across academia, business, and government, and why Africa currently outranks Europe and North America on representation.

events.title: Political Mistrust and its Causes
events.description: Two political trust researchers explain how mistrust differs from distrust, why civic education and life experience shape it, and what falling trust means for democracy and rising populism.

events.title: Pluralistic Logic
events.description: Whether logic has one correct system or many, and how a philosopher defends the idea that competing logics can each be valid on their own terms.

events.title: Understanding Glaciers through Satellites
events.description: A researcher explains how satellite radar imagery reveals glacier zones and melt patterns in the Arctic, and why correcting that data accurately matters for tracking water resources and climate change.

events.title: What is Quantum Computing?
events.description: How quantum bits can hold multiple states at once, why that makes certain problems like simulating materials or factoring huge numbers newly solvable, and what still stands between today's lab-bound qubits and a working machine.

events.title: What is an Equal City?
events.description: How rising tourism and unchecked property markets are pricing residents out of cities like Venice and Amsterdam, and whether philosophy can explain why gentrification is actually unjust.

events.title: Our Revolution for the Orient
events.description: How Soviet newspapers spun Iran's 1979 Islamic Revolution to fit communist ideology, quietly downplaying its religious roots to preserve the story of inevitable progress toward revolution.

events.title: The Evolution of Depression
events.description: How evolutionary mismatch between ancestral hunter-gatherer life and modern city living—diet, exercise, social media, individualism—may explain rising rates of depression, anxiety, and stress.

events.title: Conspiracy Theories as a Political Tool
events.description: How political actors exploit conspiracy theories by weaponizing their flexibility against evidence, and how belief in a secret plot builds trust networks that shift from personal skepticism into extremist ideology.

events.title: Sexual Double Standards
events.description: How the sexual double standard shapes what we expect from men and women in bed, why it persists even when people privately disagree, and what media could do to change it.

events.title: A Logical Brain
events.description: How logic, algebra, and geometry intersect, and why a mathematician studying formal reasoning turned to polyhedral shapes to model three-dimensional space.

events.title: Menstruation in Space
events.description: How researcher Marion Dugué is developing a menstrual cup for zero gravity, and why she believes menstrual blood could become a resource for regenerative medicine on long space missions.

events.title: Coral Reefs
events.description: How coral animals build reef skeletons and host algae, and how scientists are testing whether corals can gain heat tolerance as marine heatwaves drive worsening bleaching.
